description: The spec for the spec harness itself. The harness holds its own work to the discipline it enforces on everyone else's: these requirements are the source of truth, the tagged Cucumber scenarios under tests/features are their executable form, and tests/spec_completeness.rs fails the build if the two drift apart. Point the harness at itself with spec --root harness.

requirements.title: Refactoring is refused on a red bar
requirements.story: As a developer held to the discipline by tooling, I want the Red/Green/Refactor phase tracked from the test runs themselves so that a refactor can never begin while the bar is red.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a fresh TDD session, when a failing test run is recorded, then the phase is "RED"
Given a fresh TDD session, when a passing test run is recorded, then the phase is "GREEN"
Given a session whose last run failed, when a refactor is attempted, then the refactor is refused with a message containing "Never refactor on a red bar"
Given a session whose last run passed, when a refactor is started, then the phase is "REFACTOR"

requirements.title: Structural problems in the spec are reported as exact issues
requirements.story: As a developer driving work from a requirements spec, I want structural problems reported as exact, actionable issues so that only a usable spec is ever turned into scenarios and code.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a criterion that names no starting state, action and result, when the spec is validated, then the verdict is "invalid"
Given a well-formed pending requirement, when the spec is validated, then the verdict is "valid"

Given an implemented requirement whose feature file carries none of its tags, when the spec is validated, then an issue reads "REQ-006: no scenario tagged @REQ-006 in features/x.feature - implemented requirements need executable scenarios"
Given two requirements sharing one id, when the spec is validated, then an issue reads "REQ-001: duplicate id - every requirement needs its own"

requirements.title: Vague wording is rejected before any code exists
requirements.story: As a developer agreeing a spec with an agent, I want ambiguous wording called out one finding at a time so that a valid-but-vague requirement is reworded before a single test is generated from it.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a story naming no actor, no benefit and three ambiguous words, when the requirement is refined, then there are 5 findings
Given a story that opens without an actor, when the requirement is refined, then a finding reads "story: missing the actor - start with 'As a ...' so we know who this is for"
Given a story and criteria naming an actor, a benefit, a concrete outcome and an edge case, when the requirement is refined, then the verdict is "clean"
Given a vague rewording written over a clean requirement, when the requirement is refined, then the verdict is "not clean"

requirements.title: Authored changes are written straight to the project's files
requirements.story: As a developer whose project the harness is editing, I want every authored change written straight to the file it belongs in so that my editor, my build, and git diff see it the moment it is made.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a feature file created through the work tree, when the working tree is read, then the working tree file contains "Feature: Calc"
Given a file that does not exist yet, when it is written, then the write is reported as a "create"
Given a path that escapes the project root, when it is written, then the write is refused
Given a path inside the harness's own .spec directory, when it is written, then the write is refused

requirements.title: Each command is offered only the tools that step of the loop needs
requirements.story: As a developer running an LLM-backed command, I want that caller offered a named subset of the tool catalog so that the model stays on task and cannot write a file unless the step calls for it.
acceptanceCriteria: Given the default profiles, when every one of them is inspected, then the only caller offered command_run is "implement"
Given the default profiles, when every one of them is inspected, then 0 of them offer a tool that writes
Given the caller "spec-draft", when its tools are listed offline, then the offered tools are "list_requirements, get_requirement, validate_spec, refine_requirement"
Given a config naming an invalid tool, when the tools are listed offline, then the offered tools exclude "nope_tool"

requirements.title: Every build tool's report becomes one summary shape
requirements.story: As a developer running the loop in any supported language, I want each build tool's report parsed into a single summary shape so that the RED and GREEN phases are computed the same way everywhere.
acceptanceCriteria: Given cargo test output whose result lines span two binaries, when the output is parsed, then the parsed run has 8 tests, 1 failures, 0 errors, 2 skipped
Given a Surefire report of 3 tests with 1 failure, when the report is parsed, then the parsed run has 3 tests, 1 failures, 0 errors, 1 skipped
Given a build that fails before any test runs, when the output is parsed, then the parsed run has 0 tests, 0 failures, 1 errors, 0 skipped
Given a project whose runtime is absent, when the tests are run, then the run is refused and the refusal names "mvn"

requirements.title: Every next action starts from the spec, not from guesswork
requirements.story: As an agent driving the workflow, I want to list the requirements and read one enriched with its file locations so that the next action is chosen from the catalog rather than from a chat transcript.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a pending requirement and an implemented one, when the requirements are listed, then 2 requirements are listed with their ids, titles and statuses
Given a requirement that lives in an included file, when the requirements are listed, then the listing names that file as its "specFile"
Given a known requirement id, when the requirement is shown, then the reply names feature location "features/x.feature" and a workflow hint naming "@REQ-001"
Given an unknown requirement id, when the requirement is shown, then the reply is an error reading "No requirement with id 'REQ-999'. Call list_requirements to see valid ids."

requirements.title: A requirement cannot be marked implemented without proof
requirements.story: As a developer who owns the spec wording, I want drafting, status flips and scenario edits gated before they reach the file so that the catalog stays a reviewed source of truth rather than a record of what an agent felt like doing.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a session whose last run failed, when a requirement is marked implemented, then the flip is refused
Given a green bar and a scenario carrying the requirement's tag, when the requirement is marked implemented, then the written spec names "features/calc.feature" as the feature file
Given a green bar and no scenario carrying the tag, when the requirement is marked implemented, then the flip is refused and the message names the recovery commands
Given a draft the developer declines, when the wizard finishes, then the spec file still holds 1 requirement

requirements.title: Generated tests are written to the project and fall back to a template
requirements.story: As a developer generating step definitions and unit tests, I want a deterministic template as the floor and model output used only after it validates so that a generation step can degrade but never break the run.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a project with no model resolved, when step definitions are generated, then the generation is written from "template"
Given invalid model output, when step definitions are generated, then the generation is written from "template" rather than the model reply
Given a requirement carrying acceptance criteria, when a unit test is generated, then the written test fails
Given a feature whose every step is already defined, when step definitions are generated, then the generation is refused

requirements.title: A project's ecosystems are detected and nothing is installed
requirements.story: As a developer pointing the harness at a project, I want its ecosystems detected from marker files and each runtime's presence reported so that execution is attempted only where a runtime already exists.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a project containing "Cargo.toml", when the project is inspected, then the language "Rust" is detected with framework "cucumber-rs" and runtime "cargo"
Given a project containing "pom.xml", when the project is inspected, then the language "Java" is detected with framework "Cucumber-JVM" and runtime "mvn"
Given a project whose runtime is missing, when the project is inspected, then execution is disabled and authoring stays "available"
Given an empty directory, when the project is inspected, then the reply lists 5 supported ecosystems

requirements.title: Undefined steps are found without running anything
requirements.story: As a developer about to scaffold step definitions, I want the steps that have no matching definition found by parsing the sources so that the gap is known without executing or installing anything.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a Java project where one step of three carries a definition, when the missing steps are reported, then 2 steps are missing
Given a Java project whose definitions are written as Cucumber expressions, when the missing steps are reported, then 0 steps are missing
Given a Java project carrying step definitions, when the missing steps are reported, then the report names framework "Cucumber-JVM"

requirements.title: One catalog is the entry point to a backlog spread over many files
requirements.story: As a developer growing a spec beyond one file, I want the root catalog to include child spec files so that the backlog scales while a single entry point still drives the workflow.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a root catalog that includes a child spec file, when the requirements are listed, then 2 requirements merge into one backlog
Given an include naming a file that is absent from disk, when the spec is validated, then the verdict is "invalid"
Given includes that refer back to one another, when the spec is validated, then the cycle is reported as an error
Given a requirement that lives in an included file, when it is marked implemented, then the flip is written back to the file it lives in and 0 other spec files change

requirements.title: A test run narrows to the target that owns the feature
requirements.story: As a developer running one requirement's tests, I want the run narrowed to the test target that owns its feature file so that the bar I am watching is not buried under every other target in the crate.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a crate whose tests directory holds "tdd_state.rs", when the tests are run for feature "tests/features/tdd_state.feature", then the run is scoped to "--test tdd_state"
Given a crate whose tests directory holds only "cucumber.rs", when the tests are run for feature "tests/features/tdd_state.feature", then the run is scoped to "--test cucumber"
Given a crate whose tests directory is missing any target that matches, when the tests are run for that feature, then the run carries no "--test" flag

requirements.title: A drafted requirement carries the prefix its catalog already uses
requirements.story: As a developer drafting into a spec that already numbers its requirements, I want the new id to carry the prefix the catalog uses so that one binary serves every spec without being told how each one numbers.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a catalog whose highest id is "HARNESS-014", when a requirement is drafted, then the draft is written as "HARNESS-015"
Given an empty catalog holding 0 requirements, when a requirement is drafted, then the draft is written as "REQ-001"
Given a catalog whose highest id is "REQ-0007", when a requirement is drafted, then the draft is written as "REQ-0008"
Given a catalog numbering "HARNESS-001" that also includes a file numbering "CLI-099", when a requirement is drafted, then the draft is written as "HARNESS-002"
Given a catalog whose highest id is "HARNESS-014", when the status is reported, then the next id is "HARNESS-015"
Given a catalog holding "HARNESS-014", when the delivery target "harness-014" is read, then the target is requirement "HARNESS-014"

requirements.title: The project is found by walking up from the working directory
requirements.story: As a developer running spec from inside a repository, I want the nearest enclosing project used when none is named so that the command works on what I am looking at without a flag.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a project whose catalog sits at its root, when the root is discovered from "src/domain" inside it, then the reported root is the directory holding "requirements/requirements.json"
Given a project nested inside another project, when the root is discovered from "harness/src", then the reported root is "harness"
Given a directory holding ".spec" and no catalog, when the root is discovered from "src" inside it, then the reported root is the directory holding ".spec"
Given a directory that is itself the project root, when the root is discovered from it, then 0 roots are reported
Given a directory whose every ancestor is missing both markers, when the root is discovered from it, then 0 roots are reported

requirements.title: An undirected draft lands in the catalog file covering the working directory
requirements.story: As a developer drafting in a catalog split across files, I want a requirement to land in the spec file covering the directory I am in so that the backlog stays organised without my naming a file every time.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a catalog including "core/math.json" and a command run in "core", when a requirement is drafted with no file named, then "requirements/core/math.json" holds 2 requirements
Given a command run in "src/domain", for which a covering spec file is missing, when a requirement is drafted with no file named, then "requirements/requirements.json" holds 2 requirements
Given a catalog including "core/math.json" and a command run in "core", when a requirement is drafted naming "requirements/requirements.json", then the draft is written as "REQ-002"

requirements.title: A generating run offers the developer a branch of its own before it writes
requirements.story: As a developer about to let a generating run author real files, I want the run to offer me a branch of its own once before it writes anything so that the whole run is one thing I can keep, merge, or throw away.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a git repository on "main", when the branch gate is answered "newline support", then the branch "spec/newline-support" is created
Given a git repository on "main", when the branch gate is answered with an empty line, then the created branch starts with "spec/"
Given a git repository on "main", when the branch gate is answered "n", then 0 branches are created
Given a run started with --no-branch, when the branch gate runs, then the developer is asked 0 questions
Given a project that is not a git repository, when the branch gate runs, then the warning names "no undo"
Given a git repository on "main" holding uncommitted work, when the branch gate runs, then the warning names "uncommitted work" before the question
Given a git repository on "main", when the branch gate is answered "bad..name", then 0 branches are created and the warning names "not a usable branch name"
Given a git repository on "main" where creating a branch fails, when the branch gate is answered "newlines", then 0 branches are created and the warning names "main" as the branch the run stays on
Given a git repository on "main" and no one left to answer, when the branch gate runs, then 0 branches are created

requirements.title: Every run belongs to a GUID session that can be resumed by id
requirements.story: As a developer returning to a project, I want each run of the harness to belong to a GUID-identified session that I can resume by id so that the TDD state and project memory I pick up are the ones I left.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a project with no sessions on record, when the shell session starts, then the session shown is "new" and its id is a GUID of 36 characters
Given a session recorded on GREEN, when the shell session starts with that session id, then the session shown is "resumed" with phase "GREEN"
Given 2 sessions on record, when the shell session starts, then the session list names 3 sessions with the current one marked "*" and 0 questions are asked
Given a state file written before sessions existed holding 2 entries, when the shell session starts, then the adopted session keeps 2 entries
Given a session id that is not on record, when the shell session starts with that session id, then the start is refused naming ".spec/state.json"
Given a malformed session id "not-a-guid", when the shell session starts with that session id, then the start is refused naming "not a GUID"
Given a current session on RED, when the TDD state is read in a fresh invocation without a session id, then the persisted phase is "RED"
Given a current session remembering module root "kata", when a new shell session starts, then the new session's memory names module root "kata"

requirements.title: A request is preserved as an ask and broken into requirements that point back at it
requirements.story: As a developer whose request becomes several requirements, I want the request kept word for word as an ask_requirement in requirements.json and every requirement derived from it linked both ways so that nothing of what I asked is lost in the breakdown and each requirement can be traced to it.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a request "sum numbers from a comma separated string, empty input means zero" and a model splitting it into 2 requirements, when it is broken down without prompts, then the ask has type "ask_requirement", its request field is exactly "sum numbers from a comma separated string, empty input means zero", and it derives 2 requirements
Given an ask deriving "REQ-002" and "REQ-003", when each derived requirement is read, then its type is "actionable_requirement" and its parent is "ASK-001"
Given a request already broken down into 2 requirements, when the same request is broken down again, then the spec file has 4 requirements and its bytes equal the bytes before the second run
Given a request "make the calculator nicer" and no model, when it is broken down without prompts, then 0 requirements are derived and the ask carries 1 blocking question

Given a requirement "REQ-001" that was never part of an ask, when another request is broken down, then the row written for "REQ-001" has 0 of the keys type, request, parent, derived, decomposition, acceptance, proposals, questions

requirements.title: Acceptance of a derived requirement is recorded by who gave it and follows its wording
requirements.story: As a developer deciding what gets built, I want every derived requirement to record whether the rules or I accepted it, to lose that acceptance when its meaning changes, and to be decidable by number without a wizard so that my vote is never substituted by the agent's judgment and a reworded requirement is never implemented on an acceptance it no longer has.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a request broken down without prompts, when a proposal passes the rules, then its requirement carries an acceptance whose by is "automatic"
Given a request broken down without prompts, when a proposal has a criterion the rules refuse as unphrased, then that proposal's status is "pending" and 0 requirements are written for it
Given an ask with a proposal left pending by the rules, when a decision accepts it with by "automatic", then the decision is refused with "cannot be accepted automatically"
Given an ask with a proposal left pending by the rules, when a decision accepts it with by "user", then its requirement carries an acceptance whose by is "user"
Given a derived requirement accepted automatically, when its title is changed to "Sums numbers separated by commas or newlines", then its acceptance is removed and its ask's ready flag is false
Given a derived requirement accepted automatically, when its title is changed only in whitespace to "Comma   separated numbers are summed", then its acceptance still has by "automatic"
Given an interactive breakdown of 1 proposal, when the developer answers "" at the vote, then the developer is told "An empty answer is not a vote." and the proposal's status is still "pending"

Given an interactive breakdown with 1 requirement accepted, when the developer answers "n" to the coverage question, then the ask's state is "open" and its readiness reason is "the user has not confirmed the accepted requirements cover the request"
Given an ask with 1 accepted requirement, when a decision confirms coverage with by "automatic", then the decision is refused with "user's decision"

requirements.title: An ask is ready for implementation only when every derived requirement is accepted and nothing is open
requirements.story: As a developer about to implement, I want an ask's readiness derived from its derived requirements, its open questions, and its proposals rather than declared so that no requirement is implemented while the breakdown it belongs to is still undecided.
acceptanceCriteria: Given an ask whose 2 derived requirements are accepted, whose decomposition is complete, and which has 0 open blocking questions, when its readiness is read, then its ready flag is true
Given an ask with 1 accepted requirement and 1 blocking question unanswered, when its readiness is read, then its ready flag is false with the reason "question 1 is blocking and unanswered"
Given an ask with 1 accepted requirement and 1 blocking question, when the question is answered "only the comma", then its ready flag is true

Given an interactive breakdown of 2 proposals, when the developer approves proposal 1 and rejects proposal 2, then the ask derives 1 requirement and its ready flag is false with the reason "proposal 2 \"Empty string returns zero\" was rejected and neither revised nor excluded"
Given an interactive breakdown of 2 proposals, when the developer approves proposal 1 and excludes proposal 2, then the ask derives 1 requirement and its ready flag is true
Given a ready ask with 2 derived requirements, when one derived requirement is deleted, then the ask derives 1 requirement, its proposal's status is "pending", and its ready flag is false
Given an ask that derives "REQ-002", when the ask is deleted without cascade, then the deletion is refused with "ASK-001 derives REQ-002"
Given an ask that derives "REQ-002", when the ask is deleted with cascade, then the spec has 0 rows for "ASK-001" and 0 rows for "REQ-002"

requirements.title: Explain one spec command by name - what it does, its options, and the
requirements.story: As a requester, I want "explain one spec command by name - what it does, its options, and the tools it may call - discovered from the binary's own command tree, and list every command when none is named" so that every requirement derived from it is delivered.
acceptanceCriteria: Given the ask ASK-001, when HARNESS-023 "Explain specific command by name" is implemented, then the derived requirement HARNESS-023 has the status "implemented"
Given the ask ASK-001, when HARNESS-024 "List all commands when no name is specified" is implemented, then the derived requirement HARNESS-024 has the status "implemented"
Given the ask ASK-001 with a derived requirement still pending, when spec mark-implemented ASK-001 runs, then it is refused with "is still pending"
requirements.request: explain one spec command by name - what it does, its options, and the tools it may call - discovered from the binary's own command tree, and list every command when none is named

proposals.title: Explain specific command by name
proposals.story: As a CLI user, I want to retrieve the documentation for a named command so that I can learn its description, options, and tool dependencies.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a valid command name "run" exists in the command tree, when the explain command is called with "run", then the output displays the command's description, its options, and the list of tools it calls
Given the command name "unknown-cmd" does not exist in the command tree, when the explain command is called with "unknown-cmd", then an error message "Unknown command" is returned
findings: criterion "Given a valid command name "run" exists in the command tree, when the explain command is called with "run", then the output displays the command's description, its options, and the list of tools it calls": the outcome is not concrete - state the exact expected value after 'then'

proposals.title: List all commands when no name is specified
proposals.story: As a CLI user, I want to see a full list of available commands so that I can discover all capabilities without guessing command names.
acceptanceCriteria: Given no command name is provided, when the explain command is called, then the output lists every available command name from the command tree
Given the command tree is empty, when the explain command is called with no name, then the output is an empty list
findings: criterion "Given no command name is provided, when the explain command is called, then the output lists every available command name from the command tree": the outcome is not concrete - state the exact expected value after 'then'
